A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OAT/OctreeGPT research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Relocated material and renumbered equations and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-reconstruction and generation experiments in Tables 1–3, plus adaptive-subdivision, token-length, and octree-ordering ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds resource measurements, architecture ablations, and reconstruction comparisons in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same quadric-driven subdivision, Perceiver tokenizer, hierarchical residual quantization, losses, and OctreeGPT generation procedure. The new architecture variants are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions describe Objaverse-based shape reconstruction and text-conditioned shape generation. The added appendix experiments and replacement qualitative examples introduce no identified new dataset, domain, task, or test population.

E2.justification: v2 adds quantitative and qualitative reconstruction comparisons against Trellis and Dora, including three Dora token budgets, in Table 8 and Figure 10. These works were only cited in v1, so this materially expands the evaluated reconstruction alternatives. Existing reconstruction and generation comparators remain; OctGPT is discussed but not benchmarked.

E3.justification: The original splits, preprocessing, training settings, and main evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Added protocols include generation-efficiency measurements at two quadric thresholds, a 100K-point octree-construction benchmark, and memory measurement. The concurrent comparison specifies rendered textured images for Trellis and a 64K-point input for the highest-resolution Dora variant.

E4.justification: v1 already studies adaptive subdivision, token length, and node ordering. v2 substantially extends component validation with convolution/concatenation-versus-average-pooling and hierarchy-removal ablations across reconstruction and generation (Table 7). It also adds runtime, memory, and adaptive-octree construction-overhead analyses in Appendix C.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty measures. v2 introduces ± values for generation runtime and memory in Table 4 and for octree-construction timing. Their statistical meaning, sample counts, and run or seed counts are unspecified, so additional repeated runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original node-ordering results retain their values. New results include 20.4 versus 25.6 GB memory for OctreeGPT and Craftsman-VQ+GPT, respectively; KID 13.65 without hierarchy versus 5.79 for the full model; and Table 8 CD values of 7.9 for OAT, 8.1 for Trellis, and 5.2 for 4096-token Dora, all scaled by 10^-3. Figure 9 replaces six generation examples with sixteen. These additions do not establish a matched-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The quadric definitions, minimization derivation in Appendix A, quantization algorithm, and mathematical model formulations are unchanged. Moving the final loss inline and renumbering subsequent equations are presentation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and headline claims: complexity-adaptive tokenization, approximately 50% token savings at comparable quality, better reconstruction at similar budgets, and improved downstream generation. The appendix additions supply evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets the hierarchy ablation as supporting coarse-to-fine generation and attributes construction efficiency to pruning simple regions and fast quadric computation. It also qualifies Trellis's token cost because it models appearance and identifies Dora's sampling strategy as potentially complementary. The texture limitation and societal-impact discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies an A100 GPU for resource measurements and documents input details for the added construction and concurrent-method comparisons. Appendix B's core training hyperparameters, codebook settings, token limits, and project-page link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Octree Transformer, Cube, and OctGPT, and changes the visibility-based occupancy attribution from CLAY to Cube. Appendix C expands positioning against Trellis, Dora, and OctGPT. Existing references are retained; publication and venue updates do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact. v2 makes limited prose and caption shortenings and adds focused appendix paragraphs on efficiency, architecture, and concurrent work, without extensive rewriting or restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4, 7, and 8 and Figure 10, and replaces the compact six-example Figure 9 with a full-width sixteen-example display. Existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered. Main figures and table structures remain essentially unchanged, with tighter formatting and reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the efficiency and architecture rationale through memory and construction-time measurements, hierarchy ablations, and relevant concurrent-method comparisons. These strengthen an already established empirical case while leaving the method and main results unchanged. Undefined ± statistics and incomplete documentation connecting Table 8 to the original evaluation settings limit the added evidence's interpretability.
